open_points.subject: A28 wall-clock read cardinality
open_points.text: “the wall clock gives the instant … one reading per request … (no cache, no local time, no second reading…)” contradicts “An operation reads the clock once for its own timestamps” and “The one exception is the occurred_at of an audit record appended through the audit writer: the writer takes it when it appends.”
open_points.question: Is there one shared wall-clock reading for the entire request, or may each operation involved in that request—including authorization, the owning use case, and audit_writer—take its own reading?
options: One request-scoped instant is shared by every operation and the audit writer.
Each operation reads system_clock.utc_now once, and audit_writer takes its separate reading when appending.
Only the owning use case reads once; authorization and audit receive that instant from it.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the established operation rule and explicit audit exception as controlling: each operation reads once, and audit_writer may take a separate reading.

witness.initial: An active assigned operator has a valid session and an active project with a section.
events: The operator sends one HTTP request to update the section’s progress.
The authorization path checks session expiry using the current instant.
project_tracking.set_section_progress obtains an instant for updated_at.
audit_writer.append_audit obtains an instant for AuditRecord.occurred_at.
outcomes: Under “one reading per request,” all participants must share one wall-clock value, despite the prohibition on caching and the statement that audit_writer takes its instant when appending.

Under the per-operation rule and audit exception, authorization, project_tracking, and audit_writer may make separate system_clock.utc_now calls, and SectionProgress.updated_at may differ from AuditRecord.occurred_at.
witness.observer: An administrator reading progress and audit timestamps, and clock-call-count verification tests.
